course.title: The Adventures of Pinocchio
course.learnerRule: A learner completes one selected level per session; Foundation, Core, and Studio are alternatives, not cumulative work.

story.guidingQuestionKo: 가치를 잃었다고 취급받을 때도 다시 시작할 수 있을까요?
story.synopsisKo: 당나귀가 된 피노키오는 서커스에서 착취당하고 바다에 버려지지만, 다시 나무 인형의 몸을 되찾은 뒤 거대한 상어에게 삼켜진다.

editorialPolicy.storyFidelity: The twelve sessions preserve the complete original 36-chapter arc, causal sequence, major choices, consequences, reunions, and ending.
editorialPolicy.foundation: Concrete, speakable sentences with one main action and mostly 6–11 words per line.
editorialPolicy.core: Connected sentences with cause, contrast, and reaction, mostly 10–18 words per line.
editorialPolicy.studio: Literary but performable sentences that preserve narrator wit, suspense, and moral tension.
editorialPolicy.safety: Historic peril and slapstick retain their narrative consequence without added graphic detail.
editorialPolicy.narration: Generate one continuous master per session and level; Watch and Mimic must seek within the same performance.
editorialPolicy.classTime: The story text remains concise; sixty minutes comes from deliberate replay, recording, comparison, retrieval, and sentence reconstruction—not padding the narration.

narration.direction: Treat the circus as glittering exploitation, make the sea transformation strange and liberating, and end the Shark swallowing with awe and suspense.
narration.productionRule: Generate one continuous master per session and level; Watch and Mimic seek within that exact same master.

livingStorybook.artBrief: A circular circus ring opens toward a moonlit sea: trainer, hoop, Fairy in the audience, injured donkey, drum-maker's rope and stone, fish revealing the wooden body, open water, giant Shark, and Tunny silhouette.

beats.summaryKo: 요정을 알아보지만 말 대신 울음만 나온다.
점프에 실패하자 가치 없는 상품처럼 팔린다.
새 주인은 생명이 아니라 가죽만 본다.
당나귀 껍질이 사라지고 나무 몸이 돌아온다.
삼켜진 뒤 탈출을 포기한 물고기를 만난다.

lines.text: A circus owner bought Donkey Pinocchio.
He trained him to perform difficult tricks.
The audience cheered inside the bright ring.
Pinocchio saw the Blue Fairy watching him.
He tried to call her, but only brayed.
During a jump, Pinocchio fell and became lame.
The owner sold him to another man.
The man wanted donkey skin for a drum.
He tied on a stone and drowned Pinocchio.
Underwater fish ate away the donkey body.
The wooden puppet appeared alive again.
Pinocchio escaped and swam toward an azure Goat.
The Goat called him toward a white rock.
Then the Terrible Shark opened its enormous mouth.
The Shark swallowed Pinocchio in one rush.
Inside, he met a Tunny waiting in darkness.

lines.text: A circus owner bought Donkey Pinocchio and trained him through punishment.
Soon the animal performed bows, dances, and dangerous jumps before crowds.
During one bright performance, Pinocchio recognized the Blue Fairy in the audience.
He tried to call her name, but his mouth produced only a donkey's bray.
Confused and distracted, Pinocchio missed a jump and injured one leg.
The circus owner immediately sold the lame donkey for almost nothing.
His next owner cared only about using the skin for a drumhead.
The man tied a heavy stone to Pinocchio and dropped him underwater.
Hungry fish consumed the donkey covering while the protected wooden body remained.
When the rope rose, the surprised buyer found a living marionette instead.
Pinocchio slipped free and explained that the Fairy had protected him.
While he swam away, an azure Goat called from a white rock.
Before he could reach safety, the Terrible Shark appeared nearby.
Its mouth opened like a cave and pulled the swimmer inward.
Pinocchio was swallowed before he could change direction.
In the darkness, a large Tunny explained that escape seemed impossible.

lines.text: A circus owner purchased Donkey Pinocchio and converted the consequences of Toyland into a profitable performance.
Training replaced play with punishment until the animal could bow, dance, and leap through dangerous hoops.
During one glittering show, Pinocchio recognized the Blue Fairy watching from the crowded seats.
He attempted to call to her, but the human appeal emerged as nothing more than a humiliating bray.
Distracted by recognition and shame, Pinocchio missed a jump, fell heavily, and permanently injured one leg.
The owner who had valued his tricks sold the lame animal immediately for a handful of coins.
The second buyer saw no living creature at all, only a hide that could become a drumhead.
He fastened a stone to the donkey and lowered him into the sea to end the transaction efficiently.
Beneath the water, fish consumed the donkey covering while the Fairy's protection preserved the wooden marionette inside.
The rope returned not with a dead animal but with Pinocchio alive in his original wooden body.
He broke away from the astonished buyer, explaining that the Fairy had sent the fish to protect him.
As he swam through open water, an azure Goat called urgently from a white rock.
Relief lasted only until the Terrible Shark surfaced and opened a mouth large enough to resemble a cavern.
The rushing water defeated Pinocchio's strongest swimming and carried him directly toward the monster.
In a single motion the Shark swallowed him, replacing the open sea with complete darkness.
There Pinocchio met a resigned Tunny who had stopped believing that anyone could leave alive.
